title: Design a Distributed Model Training System
prompt: Design a system for training a large neural network across hundreds or thousands of GPUs spanning many machines, that can recover cleanly from individual node/GPU failures during a multi-week training run.
requirements: Functional: distribute a training job across many GPUs/nodes, checkpoint progress periodically, resume from a checkpoint after a failure
Non-functional: training runs for weeks, so failures are expected and must not lose more than a small amount of progress; should scale near-linearly with more GPUs up to a point
discussion_points: Parallelism strategy: data parallelism vs. model/tensor parallelism vs. pipeline parallelism, and when each is needed
Gradient synchronization across nodes (all-reduce) and the network bandwidth it demands
Checkpointing strategy: how often, where checkpoints are stored, and how large they can get for a big model
Failure detection and recovery: what happens to an in-flight training step when one GPU dies mid-batch
Straggler nodes slowing down synchronous training, and options for mitigating that
How this differs for fine-tuning a smaller model vs. pretraining a frontier-scale one
